title: Supercomputer Predicts Final Champions League Table Halfway Through League Phase
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda LangellNov 4, 2026Matheus Cunha rescued Manchester United’s league phase campaign. / Molly Darlington/Getty ImagesThe first half of the 2026–27 Champions League league phase is done and dusted, and only two perfect teams remain: defending cup holders Paris Saint-Germain and 15-time European champions Real Madrid.

The two European giants sit atop the league phase standings, comfortably looking down at the other 34 teams competing for a knockout stage berth. PSG waltzed to a 6–0 victory over Villarreal to collect their fourth win in the competition, while Los Blancos needed another vintage comeback to squeak out a 3–2 victory over AEK Athens.
The two games told a larger story of Matchday 4. Across Europe’s premier club competition, there were goals galore, epic come-from-behind victories and strong performances from unexpected contenders.

Manchester United snapped a nine-game winless run with a late surge against Roma, while Liverpool were once again upended in Istanbul. Como then put a staggering nine goals past Lens and debutants Viking secured their first win on Europe’s biggest stage.
The league phase standings are slowly taking shape, and the Opta supercomputer brings a new round of predictions that spell out success for 24 teams and bitter damnation for 12.

Unsurprisingly, the supercomputer backs PSG and Real Madrid to finish as the top two teams in the league phase. Both clubs have won all four of their opening matches and are expected to cruise into the last 16 with close to 20 points each.

Close behind are Arsenal and Bayern Munich. The two teams previously traded blows in a 2–2 draw back in October, the only stain on the Gunners’ league phase résumé this season. They waltzed past Slavia Prague on Wednesday, while Vincent Kompany’s men found similar success against Atlético Madrid 24 hours prior.

Bayern Munich are expected to finish with around 16 points, much like Barcelona and Manchester City. All three teams are virtually interchangeable as it stands in Opta’s final table, but the defending Spanish champions’ upcoming date with the Cityzens could shake up the standings.

Rounding out the top eight are Liverpool and Aston Villa. Both sides walked away with zero points from Matchday 4, but the supercomputer still projects the Premier League foes to automatically progress to the round of 16.
The bad news for Unai Emery’s men is they still must face PSG, whereas the Reds have a fairly favorable schedule on the horizon, with a match at Inter their biggest test left in the league phase.
Matheus Cunha led Manchester United to victory over Roma. / Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty ImagesPosition

Although finishing in the top eight is every team’s goal, staying out the bottom 12 is the next best thing. The clubs that finish in ninth to 24th place will compete in a two-legged tie in the knockout phase playoffs, with the victors progressing to the round of 16.

A few surprise names litter Opta’s mid-table predictions. Three of the four Champions League debutants—Como, LASK and Viking—are projected to survive the league phase. Cesc Fàbregas’s men will be dreaming of sneaking into the top eight, but they surely will still be satisfied with a potential 10th place finish.

With how they’ve performed recently, Manchester United are another unexpected club projected to advance to the knockout phase playoffs. The Red Devils couldn’t buy a win in any competition until they shocked Roma on Tuesday, resurrecting their floundering Champions League campaign.

Speaking of Roma, they will feel like they deserve to be much higher than 19th place. The Italian outfit was in the driver’s seat to beat both Real Madrid and United, but collapsed in both games to weigh down its record this season.
Atlético Madrid’s relationship with elite strikers runs deep. pic.twitter.com/Ju3qRRr23B

Atlético Madrid will hope to prove Opta wrong as well. Should they collect just their projected 11 points, it would be a massive disappointment considering they were semifinalists last season. It would also be a poor indictment of Diego Simeone’s men if La Liga foe Real Betis, who are playing Champions League soccer for the first time since 2005–06, finish above them in the league phase standings.

A similar battle exists between Süper Lig rivals Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe. The supercomputer has both Turkish clubs finishing with around 10 points, which would be enough for both to appear in the knockout phase playoffs. As Liverpool can attest, playing in Istanbul is a fate every team will hope to avoid.
